{{nihongo|'''Kawasukune Shrine (Higashiagatsuma)'''|甲波宿禰神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kōzuke Province]].

=== History ===

Prefecture Regional Revitalization Department, Cultural Properties Protection Division|2022|pp=332–335}}.

Interpreting “Kōha” as “river” and “Sukune” as “straight root,” the shrine name is understood to mean “the main current of the river.” Because three shrines with “shima” (island) in their place names—Hakojima, {{ill|Takeuchi Shrine|Q66085129|qid=Q66085129|lt=Sobajima}}, and Kawashima—were aligned along the {{ill|Agatsuma River|Q1636255|qid=Q1636255}}, {{ill|Kisao Ozaki|Q21698487|qid=Q21698487}} explains that the river itself was deified<ref>{{Cite book|ja |title=Research on the Jōzuke Province Jinmyōchō |date=1974-12-10 |year=1974 |publisher=Ozaki-sensei Book Publication Society |pages=210–212 |last=Ozaki |first=Kizao |author-link=Kizao Ozaki |doi=10.11501/12266236}}{{Registration required}}</ref>.

During the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת סנגוקו|hu|Hadakozó fejedelemségek kora (Japán)|id|Zaman Sengoku|is|Sengoku-öldin|it|Periodo Sengoku|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|ka|სენგოკუს პერიოდი|kk|Сэнгоку дәуірі|ko|센고쿠 시대|lt|Sengoku laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Sengoku|nl|Sengokuperiode|no|Sengoku-perioden|pl|Sengoku (okres)|pt|Período Sengoku|ro|Perioada Sengoku|ru|Период Сэнгоку|sh|Sengoku razdoblje|simple|Sengoku period|sk|Obdobie Sengoku|sq|Periudha Sengoku|sr|Сенгоку период|sv|Sengoku|th|ยุคเซ็งโงกุ|tl|Panahong Sengoku|tr|Sengoku Dönemi|uk|Період Сенґоку|ur|سینگوکو دور|uz|Sengoku davri|vi|Thời kỳ Chiến Quốc (Nhật Bản)|wuu|战国时代（日本）|zh|战国时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, the shrine was revered by the {{ill|Nagao clan|Q1655561|qid=Q1655561}}, lords of {{ill|Shirai Castle|Q11579353|qid=Q11579353}}, and it is said that {{ill|Nagao Kageharu|Q247926|qid=Q247926}} dedicated a sword{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}.

In {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 4 ({{ill|1664|Q7581|qid=Q7581}}), it possessed shrine lands of 1 tan 3 se 25 bu of rice fields and 1 tan 7 se 4 bu of dry fields as a Daimyōjin shrine{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was called “Sukune Daimyōjin,” but in the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}} it was renamed Kawasukune Shrine{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}{{Sfn|Gunma Prefecture Regional Revitalization Department, Cultural Properties Protection Division|2022|pp=332–335}}. Until the Edo period, rituals were conducted by the head priest of Manpuku-ji, the shrine’s {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755|lt=administrative temple}}, but since the Meiji period they have been conducted by Shinto priests{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}{{Sfn|Gunma Prefecture Regional Revitalization Department, Cultural Properties Protection Division|2022|pp=332–335}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 1 ({{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}), all old records were lost in a fire at the shrine office{{Sfn|Gunma Prefecture Regional Revitalization Department, Cultural Properties Protection Division|2022|pp=332–335}}.

Based on architectural style, the main hall is estimated to date from the early 18th century, and the worship hall from the late 18th century{{Sfn|Gunma Prefecture Regional Revitalization Department, Cultural Properties Protection Division|2022|pp=332–335}}.

=== Enshrined Deities ===
The following two water deities are enshrined{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}{{Sfn|Gunma Prefecture Regional Revitalization Department, Cultural Properties Protection Division|2022|pp=332–335}}.
* {{ill|Hayakitsuhiko and Hayakitsuhime|fr|Hayakitsuhiko et Hayakitsuhime|ja|ハヤアキツヒコ・ハヤアキツヒメ|ko|하야아키츠히코・하야아키츠히메|simple|Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime|zh|速秋津日子神與速秋津比賣神|qid=Q11326733|lt=Hayaakitsuhiko-no-Kami}}
* {{ill|Hayakitsuhiko and Hayakitsuhime|fr|Hayakitsuhiko et Hayakitsuhime|ja|ハヤアキツヒコ・ハヤアキツヒメ|ko|하야아키츠히코・하야아키츠히메|simple|Hayaakitsuhiko and Hayaakitsuhime|zh|速秋津日子神與速秋津比賣神|qid=Q11326733|lt=Hayaakitsuhime-no-Kami}}

There are 58 subsidiary shrines within the precincts{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}.

* Shinmei Shrine
* Ise Shrines – 3
* Sai Shrine – 3
* Yama Shrine – 17
* Inari Shrines – 10
* Water Deity Shrines – 2
* Kasuga Shrine
* Hachiman Shrines – 2
* Ōshima Shrines – 5
* Akiba Shrines – 3
* Mishima Shrine
* Suwa Shrine
* Yasaka Shrines – 2
* Taga Shrine
* Sugawara Shrine
* Kotohira Shrine
* Agatsuma Shrines – 2
* Afuri Shrine
* Ontake Shrine

=== Cultural Properties ===
=== Higashiagatsuma Town Designated Important Cultural Properties ===
* Carvings and {{ill|Mikoshi|Q979940|qid=Q979940|lt=portable shrine}} of Kawasukune Shrine (designated March 23, Shōwa 48)<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=List of Town-Designated Cultural Properties |url=https://www.town.higashiagatsuma.gunma.jp/www/contents/1447054044287/index.html |website=Higashiagatsuma Town, Gunma Prefecture |access-date=2024-08-21 |language=ja}}</ref> – The mikoshi is said to date from {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 3 ({{ill|1575|Q6688|qid=Q6688}}){{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|pp=674–676}}.

=== Higashiagatsuma Town Designated Natural Monuments ===
* Large {{ill|Zelkova serrata|Q920344|qid=Q920344|lt=keyaki}} tree of Kawasukune Shrine (designated March 23, Shōwa 48)<ref name=":0" /> – Said to be over 700 years old; there are five other zelkova trees of similar age within the precincts{{Sfn|Azuma Village History Compilation Committee|1965|p=891}}.
